evidence.observation: Menu card is up; Enter is pressed and the card clears into play.
evidence.riff: The start card states the whole contract before you touch anything: one jump, no double jump, unlimited retries.

evidence.observation: Right is held; the courier accelerates and the lamp wedge widens as it reaches speed.
evidence.riff: Speed is a readout here — the light cone widening is the only running cue that does not depend on colour.

evidence.observation: One jump, fixed height, no double jump available.
evidence.riff: Everything downstream is built on this single unchanged number: a 56 pixel rise.

evidence.observation: Four jumps clear the starter's two gaps and its steps; geometry below x=960 is byte-identical to the starter.
evidence.riff: Leaving this section untouched is what keeps the starter's own coyote and spike fixtures valid as regression evidence.

evidence.observation: The starter's three-spike cluster at x=320 is jumped and cleared.
evidence.riff: The original hazard still reads and still kills; it is the baseline the new trap is measured against.

evidence.observation: The fork sign is on screen: UP three tight landings, ACROSS no headroom and one committed gap.
evidence.riff: Both costs are stated before the player commits — an earlier build hid this inside the corridor where the courier walked over the text.

evidence.observation: A 48 px up-jump onto ledge B, then hops to C and D: three new landings that require jumps.
evidence.riff: The measured takeoff windows are 70, 56 and 58 pixels — tight, but chosen by probe, not by feel.

evidence.observation: The coin above ledge D is taken in flight; the HUD counter turns green and reads COIN 1/1.
evidence.riff: Ledge D is the highest surface in the game and only the high line reaches it, so the coin is the high road's entire payoff.

evidence.observation: The courier jumps to clear the last spike; the spike springs upward into the jump arc and kills it.
evidence.riff: The trap is pure geometry: leaving the ground beside it is what arms it, so the naive play is the fatal one.

evidence.observation: Death card reads 'It goes up when you do'.
evidence.riff: The failure names its own cause, which is the difference between a trap and an ambush.

evidence.observation: About half a second after the death the run restarts at spawn with RETRIES reading 01.
evidence.riff: No lives and no menu: the cost of failure is time, not progress, which is what makes a lethal trap acceptable.

evidence.observation: The retried run crosses the original section again and re-enters the fork area on the floor.
evidence.riff: The low line is the one you take by doing nothing, which is why its cost has to be legible.

evidence.observation: Running beneath the high ledges with LOW / NO HEADROOM printed on the slab.
evidence.riff: A ceiling you cannot jump under is a cost you feel without being told twice.

evidence.observation: A 56 px gap is cleared from the corridor onto the merge platform.
evidence.riff: Measured takeoff window 38 pixels — the tightest required jump in the level.

evidence.observation: The courier stops short of the spike, hops straight up to spring it, lands safe, then walks underneath the raised spike.
evidence.riff: Baiting it is the whole puzzle: the same input that kills you in the air is the one that clears the path from the ground.

evidence.observation: The flag at x=1696 is reached; the completion card shows time, retries and coin 0/1 for this attempt.
evidence.riff: Coin zero on a finished run is the fork being honest — this attempt took the low line and the coin was never reachable.

evidence.observation: Enter on the completion card starts a fresh session with the retry counter back at 00.
evidence.riff: Replay resets the coin and re-arms the trap, so a second run is a real second run.

evidence.observation: Escape raises the 'Take a breath.' card and freezes the run; Enter resumes from the same position.
evidence.riff: Pause freezes the clock as well as the player, which is why the finish time stays meaningful.

evidence.observation: R restarts the attempt from spawn and the retry counter stays at 00.
evidence.riff: Choosing to restart is not failing, and the counter agrees — a small honesty in the HUD.

evidence.observation: The progress bar tracks spawn-to-finish and the coin and retry counters update live.
evidence.riff: The bar is derived from level data; the starter divided by a hard-coded 852 and saturated less than halfway along this level.
